targetAudience.primary: Architects of durable agent threads, job systems and provenance-sensitive automation
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands create, resume and fork lifecycle operations.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A long-lived work object can be resumed or derived many times, but a single mutable source label cannot distinguish stable origin, local role and parent lineage.

whyNow: A same-day merged OpenAI Codex change persists thread-source classification at creation, permits a fork to set its own source while retaining lineage, and prevents ordinary TypeScript resume from forwarding an override.

externalHook.description: Resume re-enters an existing durable identity; fork creates a new object with both a local role and a parent relationship.

coreProposition: Durable agent provenance should separate continuation-stable creation source from derivation lineage: ordinary resume must not silently relabel origin, while fork may establish a new local classification and retain its parent relation; neither label becomes authorization without an independent trust binding.

originalValue.description: Separates local creation classification from derivation lineage and identifies compatibility defaults and application-controlled labels as interpretations rather than security authority.

readerTakeaway: Define metadata by lifecycle scope, preserve creation provenance across resume, record fork lineage independently and keep descriptive labels outside authorization decisions unless bound to trusted identity.

supported: Codex persists User, Subagent, Feature(String) and MemoryConsolidation source classifications.
Fork can establish a new local source while retaining parent lineage.
The inspected TypeScript resume path suppresses a conflicting source override.
uncertain: How governed source correction should preserve history
Whether historical missing source should be Unknown in sensitive analytics

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article is a general durable-work provenance analysis and does not require a first-party project.

decisionReason: The implementation exposes a concrete lifecycle distinction and supports a reusable two-axis provenance model with explicit security boundaries.
